meta.law: Personal Data Protection Act, Cap 44 (Act No. 11 of 2022)
meta.regulations: Personal Data Protection (Collection and Processing) Regulations, 2023 (GN 449C)

dpia_triggers.a: Automated decisions with significant legal effect / profiling / sensitive data gating access
dpia_triggers.c: Processing of biometric or genetic data
dpia_triggers.d: Significant changes raising risk at any processing stage
dpia_triggers.e: Sensitive data of children or vulnerable groups
dpia_triggers.h: Systematic monitoring of public areas at scale
dpia_triggers.i: Innovative use of new technological/organizational measures
dpia_triggers.j: Processing that prevents subjects exercising their rights

controls.requirement: Organization must be registered with the PDPC as a data controller and/or processor before collecting or processing personal data.
controls.remediation: Submit Form 1 with incorporation documents and the prescribed fee to the PDPC.

controls.requirement: Organization must register under the correct capacity — controller, processor, or both — matching how it actually handles data.
controls.remediation: Determine controller vs processor role and register accordingly.

controls.requirement: Any change to registered particulars must be notified to the PDPC in writing within 14 days.
controls.remediation: Establish a process to notify the PDPC within 14 days of changes to name, address, data types, or DPO details.

controls.requirement: Registration valid 5 years; renewal applied for within 3 months before expiry, else re-registration required.
controls.remediation: Diarise certificate expiry and file Form 3 within the 3-month renewal window.

controls.requirement: Pay the registration fee matching the org size band (employees + turnover).
controls.remediation: Determine band: Small(1-49 & <100M)=100,000; Medium(50-99 & 100-500M)=200,000; Large(100+ & >500M)=1,000,000; public/religious per schedule.

controls.requirement: All personal data processed lawfully, fairly and transparently, with a lawful basis identified.
controls.evidence: Documented lawful basis per processing activity
controls.remediation: Map each processing activity to a lawful basis and document it.

controls.requirement: Data collected for explicit, specified, legitimate purposes and not used incompatibly.
controls.evidence: Purpose register; no incompatible secondary use
controls.remediation: Define and record the specific purpose for each dataset; restrict secondary use.

controls.requirement: Data collected must be adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary.
controls.remediation: Audit collected fields; remove unnecessary data; apply minimisation per Reg 28.

controls.requirement: Data collected directly from the subject, who is made aware of purposes, authorization and recipients before collection.
controls.evidence: Privacy notice shown at point of collection
controls.remediation: Deploy a collection notice at every collection point stating purpose, authorization and recipients.

controls.requirement: Personal data must not be collected by unlawful means.
controls.remediation: Review collection channels; eliminate covert or deceptive collection.

controls.requirement: Data used only for the purpose collected, save lawful s.25(2) exceptions.
controls.evidence: Use audit shows no scope creep
controls.remediation: Restrict internal use to the registered purpose; document any s.25(2) exception.

controls.requirement: Data not disclosed to anyone other than the subject except per s.25 conditions.
controls.remediation: Implement a disclosure-control policy; log and justify every external disclosure.

controls.requirement: Data accurate, kept up to date, with inaccurate data erased/rectified without delay.
controls.remediation: Implement periodic accuracy verification and a without-delay rectification workflow.

controls.requirement: Data kept in identifiable form no longer than necessary; retention periods defined.
controls.remediation: Create a retention schedule per data category with defined periods and justification.

controls.requirement: Clear internal procedures for deletion/destruction; deleted data not recoverable.
controls.remediation: Define and test secure deletion/destruction procedures ensuring irreversibility.

controls.requirement: Technical and organizational measures appropriate to risk protect data against loss, unauthorized access, alteration or processing.
controls.remediation: Implement a security baseline covering the Reg 27 factors sized to the data's risk.

controls.requirement: An operative means of managing information-security policies and procedures must exist.
controls.remediation: Adopt and maintain an information security policy with assigned ownership.

controls.requirement: Risks to personal-data security assessed and countermeasures put in place.
controls.remediation: Conduct a security risk assessment and implement controls for identified risks.

controls.requirement: Only authorized personnel may access personal data necessary for their tasks.
controls.remediation: Implement role-based access control and remove unnecessary access rights.

controls.requirement: Transfer of personal data secured against unauthorized access and changes.
controls.evidence: Encryption in transit (TLS) on data flows
controls.remediation: Enforce encryption (TLS/equivalent) on all personal-data transmissions.

controls.requirement: Storage of personal data secured against unauthorized use, access and alterations.
controls.remediation: Secure storage with access restrictions and, where feasible, encryption at rest.

controls.requirement: Backups and logs kept to the extent necessary for data security.
controls.remediation: Implement a backup schedule and retain security logs.

controls.requirement: Audit trails and event monitoring used as routine security controls.
controls.remediation: Enable audit logging and routine event monitoring/alerting.

controls.requirement: Sensitive data protected with adequate measures and, where possible, kept separate.
controls.remediation: Segregate sensitive data stores and apply enhanced protection.

controls.requirement: Procedures to detect, handle, report and learn from personal-data breaches.
controls.remediation: Establish an incident-response plan covering detection, handling, reporting and lessons-learned.

controls.requirement: Software supporting processing regularly reviewed and tested for vulnerabilities.
controls.remediation: Schedule periodic vulnerability assessments/testing of processing systems.

controls.requirement: Data-protection mechanisms and technical measures built in by design and default.
controls.remediation: Embed data-protection requirements into system design and default configurations.

controls.requirement: Controller must notify the PDPC without undue delay of any security breach affecting personal data.
controls.remediation: Add a PDPC breach-notification step (without undue delay) to the incident-response plan.

controls.requirement: Every controller and processor must appoint a DPO. No thresholds — universal.
controls.evidence: DPO appointment record; DPO details in registration
controls.remediation: Appoint a DPO (may be existing staff) and record their details, including in the PDPC registration.

controls.requirement: DPO must ensure compliance and advise on rectification of violations.
controls.remediation: Define the DPO's monitoring mandate and reporting lines internally.

controls.requirement: DPO must prepare and submit quarterly compliance reports to the PDPC.
controls.remediation: Establish a quarterly reporting cycle to the PDPC.

controls.requirement: DPO must handle applications/complaints from data subjects.
controls.remediation: Create a data-subject complaint channel managed by the DPO.

controls.requirement: Where a processor is used, a contract binds it to the controller's instructions and security standards.
controls.remediation: Put data-processing agreements in place with all processors.

controls.requirement: Subjects can obtain confirmation of processing, a description of their data, purposes, and recipients.
controls.remediation: Implement a SAR procedure with defined response steps.

controls.requirement: Subjects can require suspension of processing likely to cause substantial damage; controller acknowledges within 72 hours.
controls.remediation: Build a Form 4 handling workflow with 72-hour acknowledgement and 7-day decision.

controls.requirement: Subjects can apply (Form 5) to rectify incorrect data; controller responds within 14 days.
controls.remediation: Implement a Form 5 rectification workflow with 14-day decision and pre-amendment record retention.

controls.requirement: Subjects can apply (Form 6) to erase data on defined grounds; controller responds within 14 days, subject to exceptions.
controls.remediation: Implement a Form 6 erasure workflow including the Reg 17(4) exception checks.

controls.requirement: Subjects can require the controller to stop processing for direct marketing.
controls.remediation: Provide a direct-marketing opt-out and honour it.

controls.requirement: Where a decision significantly affecting a subject is solely automated, subject must be notified and may require human reconsideration.
controls.remediation: Notify subjects of solely-automated decisions and provide a human-reconsideration route.

controls.requirement: Org recognizes subjects' right to compensation for damage from contraventions.
controls.remediation: Document liability exposure and reference it in the data-protection policy.

controls.requirement: Where the subject is a child, special handling — representative identification, consent rules, parent/guardian informed of risks.
controls.remediation: Implement child/vulnerable-person handling per Reg 18(2).

controls.requirement: Sensitive personal data not processed without prior written consent (save s.30(5) exceptions).
controls.evidence: Written consent records for sensitive data
controls.remediation: Obtain and record prior written consent for all sensitive-data processing, or document a s.30(5) exception.

controls.requirement: Consent for sensitive data withdrawable at any time without explanation or charge.
controls.remediation: Provide a free, no-explanation consent-withdrawal mechanism.

controls.requirement: Where the subject is a minor or unable to consent, consent comes from parent/guardian/legal representative.
controls.remediation: Implement representative-consent capture for minors/incapable persons.

controls.requirement: Data not transferred outside Tanzania without a lawful basis — adequacy, transfer permit (Form 7), or s.32(4) exception.
controls.remediation: Apply for a transfer permit (Form 7) or document the adequacy/exception basis before any cross-border transfer.

controls.requirement: Where a permit is issued, transfer conditions (authorized recipient, purpose limitation, no onward transfer) honoured.
controls.remediation: Enforce permit conditions in transfer agreements and operations.

controls.requirement: Before processing likely to affect rights/freedoms, a DPIA (Form 9) must be conducted.
controls.remediation: Conduct a Form 9 DPIA for each triggering activity.

controls.requirement: Where the DPIA indicates likely impact, the controller requests PDPC instructions, attaching the report.
controls.remediation: Submit high-impact DPIA results to the PDPC and observe Reg 34 timelines.

controls.requirement: Every controller must draw up a code of ethics / data-protection policy and submit it to the PDPC for approval.
controls.remediation: Draft a data-protection code of ethics/policy and submit to the PDPC for approval.

controls.requirement: Org maintains records of processing activities (categories, purposes) to demonstrate accountability.
controls.remediation: Build and maintain a record of processing activities.

controls.requirement: Staff handling personal data trained to handle it responsibly.
controls.remediation: Run periodic data-protection awareness training.

controls.requirement: Public institutions deemed registered on commencement but must still comply fully.
controls.remediation: For public bodies — confirm deemed-registration status and ensure full substantive compliance.
